description: Commerce Department activates a seven-year denial order barring American firms from selling components to Chinese telecom maker ZTE, the first major US tech chokehold on China.
source: US Commerce Dept. press release; NYT, Apr 16 2018

description: US imposes 25% tariffs on $34 billion of Chinese imports under Section 301; Beijing retaliates immediately, formally opening the US-China trade war.
Trump administration imposes 10% tariffs on $200 billion of Chinese imports, including electronics components; China responds with duties on $60 billion of US goods.

event: Buenos Aires G20 truce; Huawei CFO arrested
description: Trump and Xi agree to a 90-day tariff truce at the G20 summit; the same day, Canada arrests Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou at US request.
Nvidia announces a $6.9 billion acquisition of Israeli networking firm Mellanox, a deal requiring Chinese antitrust approval that later becomes a lever for Beijing.
After trade talks collapse, the US raises tariffs on $200 billion of Chinese goods from 10% to 25%, rattling chip and technology stocks worldwide.
Commerce Department adds Huawei and 68 affiliates to the Entity List, requiring licenses for US technology sales and cutting the company off from American chips.
source: BIS Federal Register notice; NYT, May 15 2019

description: Google cuts Huawei off from licensed Android updates and Google apps to comply with the Entity List, showing how US export controls ripple through American tech platforms.
Commerce adds supercomputer maker Sugon, Higon and AMD joint-venture partner THATIC to the Entity List, effectively ending AMD's x86 licensing venture in China.
US adds 28 Chinese entities, including AI surveillance firms SenseTime, Megvii, Hikvision and iFlytek, to the Entity List over Xinjiang human-rights abuses.
US and China sign the Phase One trade agreement; China pledges $200 billion in extra US purchases while most existing tariffs remain in place.
China's market regulator SAMR conditionally approves Nvidia's Mellanox acquisition, requiring continued supply to Chinese customers; the conditions later underpin a 2024 antitrust probe.
Nvidia unveils the A100 data-center GPU on its Ampere architecture, its flagship AI training chip and later the first Nvidia product hit by China export limits.
source: Nvidia GTC 2020 keynote; Nvidia newsroom, May 14 2020

event: Foreign direct product rule targets Huawei
description: Commerce expands the foreign direct product rule so foreign chipmakers using US tools, including TSMC, need licenses to supply Huawei's HiSilicon designs.
TSMC announces a $12 billion chip factory in Arizona with US government support, the same day Washington tightens rules blocking its sales to Huawei.
US adds China's largest chipmaker SMIC to the Entity List, presumptively denying licenses for tools needed to make chips at 10 nanometers or below.
Nvidia introduces the H100 GPU on its Hopper architecture at GTC, a chip that becomes the workhorse of the generative-AI boom and a core export-control target.
source: Nvidia GTC 2022 keynote; Nvidia newsroom, Mar 22 2022

description: House Speaker Nancy Pelosi lands in Taipei despite Chinese warnings; Beijing launches large military drills around Taiwan, spotlighting geopolitical risk to TSMC and chip supply.
Biden signs the CHIPS and Science Act, providing $52.7 billion for US semiconductor manufacturing and barring recipients from expanding advanced chip capacity in China.

event: US orders halt to A100/H100 sales to China
description: Nvidia discloses the US now requires licenses to export A100 and H100 chips to China; AMD says its MI250 is also restricted, the first targeted AI-chip curb.
source: Nvidia Form 8-K; AMD statement; Reuters, Aug 31 2022

description: Commerce issues sweeping rules restricting exports of advanced AI chips, supercomputer items and chipmaking equipment to China, the most aggressive US tech controls to date.
source: BIS interim final rule; NYT, Oct 7 2022

description: OpenAI releases ChatGPT, igniting a global generative-AI race and an explosion in demand for Nvidia data-center GPUs that reshapes the chip-policy stakes.
With President Biden visiting its Phoenix site, TSMC raises its Arizona commitment to $40 billion and adds a second fab for 3-nanometer chips.
Nvidia forecasts quarterly revenue of $11 billion, far above estimates on AI chip demand; shares jump 24% the next day, nearing a trillion-dollar valuation.
source: Nvidia Q1 FY24 earnings; Bloomberg, May 24 2023

event: China curbs gallium and germanium exports
description: China's Commerce Ministry announces export licensing for gallium and germanium, critical chipmaking minerals, in apparent retaliation for US and allied semiconductor controls.
Huawei launches the Mate 60 Pro powered by an SMIC-made 7nm Kirin chip, surprising Washington and raising doubts about the effectiveness of export controls.
Commerce tightens AI chip rules using performance-density thresholds, blocking Nvidia's China-specific A800 and H800 chips and expanding controls to dozens more countries.
Google unveils Gemini, its most capable multimodal AI model family, trained on its in-house TPU chips, intensifying competition with OpenAI and Nvidia-based AI stacks.
AMD launches the Instinct MI300X AI accelerator at its Advancing AI event, positioning it against Nvidia's H100 and raising its 2027 AI accelerator market forecast to $400 billion.
Nvidia announces the Blackwell B200 GPU and GB200 superchip at GTC 2024, promising major performance gains for trillion-parameter AI models.
source: Nvidia GTC 2024 keynote; Nvidia newsroom, Mar 18 2024

event: Nvidia becomes world's most valuable company
description: Nvidia's market capitalization reaches about $3.34 trillion, overtaking Microsoft as the world's most valuable public company amid insatiable AI-chip demand.

event: US orders TSMC to halt AI chip shipments to China
description: Commerce orders TSMC to stop shipping 7-nanometer or more advanced AI chips to Chinese customers after a TSMC-made die was found inside a Huawei Ascend processor.

event: US curbs HBM exports, blacklists 140 firms
description: Biden administration restricts high-bandwidth memory and 24 types of chipmaking tools to China and adds 140 entities, including equipment makers, to the Entity List.

event: China opens antitrust probe into Nvidia
description: China's SAMR announces an investigation into whether Nvidia violated antimonopoly law and its Mellanox approval conditions, widely seen as retaliation for US chip curbs.
Outgoing Biden administration issues the AI Diffusion Rule, creating three tiers of countries with caps on AI chip imports; Nvidia publicly criticizes the rule.
source: BIS interim final rule; NYT, Jan 13 2025

description: Chinese startup DeepSeek's low-cost R1 open-weights model triggers a market selloff; Nvidia falls 17%, a record one-day loss, intensifying debate over compute caps.
New US 10% tariff on all Chinese imports takes effect under emergency powers; China retaliates with tariffs and export controls on tungsten and other minerals.

event: China opens antitrust probe into Google
description: Hours after new US tariffs take effect, China's SAMR announces an antitrust investigation into Google, part of a retaliation package that also targets US commodities.
At the White House, TSMC announces an additional $100 billion US investment in fabs and packaging plants, as Trump threatens tariffs on imported semiconductors.
Trump announces sweeping reciprocal tariffs, including 34% on China; escalation follows within days to 145% US and 125% Chinese tariffs, crushing chip stocks.
Nvidia discloses the US now requires licenses for H20 chips sold to China, booking a $5.5 billion charge; shares drop nearly 7% the next day.
AMD discloses new US license requirements for its MI308 AI chips sold to China and expects up to $800 million in inventory and related charges.
US and China agree in Geneva to cut tariffs for 90 days, US to 30% and China to 10%; Nvidia and chip stocks rally sharply.

event: AI Diffusion Rule rescinded; Huawei Ascend warning
description: Commerce rescinds the Biden AI Diffusion Rule and issues guidance that using Huawei Ascend AI chips anywhere in the world may violate US export controls.

event: US to allow H20 sales to China
description: Nvidia says the US government assured it licenses will be granted to resume H20 sales to China, reversing April's restriction; shares rise to records.

event: AMD cleared to resume MI308 sales
description: AMD says the Commerce Department will review its MI308 license applications favorably, allowing it to resume some China AI-chip sales alongside Nvidia's H20.

event: China summons Nvidia over H20 'backdoor' risks
description: China's Cyberspace Administration summons Nvidia over alleged tracking and remote-shutdown security risks in H20 chips, discouraging Chinese firms from buying them.
Trump says the US will impose roughly 100% tariffs on imported semiconductors, exempting companies building chip plants in America such as TSMC and Apple suppliers.
Reports confirm Nvidia and AMD agreed to pay the US government 15% of revenue from China chip sales in exchange for export licenses, an unprecedented arrangement.
Commerce revokes TSMC's validated end-user status for its Nanjing fab, requiring licenses for US equipment shipments to the China plant from year-end.

event: China finds Nvidia violated antimonopoly law
description: China's SAMR says a preliminary investigation found Nvidia violated antimonopoly law in its Mellanox acquisition, announced during US-China trade talks in Madrid.

event: China bans purchases of Nvidia RTX Pro 6000D
description: China's internet regulator reportedly orders major tech firms including ByteDance and Alibaba to stop testing and buying Nvidia's China-specific RTX Pro 6000D chips.
AMD agrees to supply OpenAI with 6 gigawatts of Instinct GPUs and grants warrants for up to 10% of AMD; shares jump about 24%.
After China expands rare-earth export controls, Trump threatens an additional 100% tariff and software export curbs; Nvidia falls nearly 5% as markets slide.
Nvidia becomes the first company valued at $5 trillion, days after Jensen Huang's Washington GTC keynote touted $500 billion in Blackwell and Rubin bookings.
Trump and Xi meet in Busan and agree to a one-year truce: US cuts fentanyl tariffs to 10%, China suspends rare-earth controls; Blackwell chips not discussed.
source: White House fact sheet; NYT, Oct 30 2025

description: Google releases Gemini 3, which tops major AI benchmarks and is trained on TPUs, boosting views that Google's in-house chips can rival Nvidia GPUs.
Reports say Meta is in talks to spend billions on Google TPUs for its data centers; Alphabet rises toward $4 trillion while Nvidia shares slip.

event: Trump approves H200 sales with 25% cut
description: Trump says Nvidia may sell H200 AI chips to approved Chinese customers, with the US government receiving 25% of revenue; Blackwell and Rubin remain barred.
source: Truth Social post; Reuters; Bloomberg, Dec 8 2025

description: Reuters reports Chinese customs agents were told Nvidia H200 chips are not permitted entry, effectively stalling sales despite Washington's new approval.
Commerce formally revises license review policy, moving Nvidia H200 and AMD MI325X exports to China from presumption of denial to case-by-case review with conditions.
source: BIS Federal Register rule; Covington; Mayer Brown, Jan 2026

description: US and Taiwan sign a trade deal cutting tariffs on Taiwanese goods, with chip tariff relief tied to $250 billion of Taiwanese semiconductor investment in America.

event: Supreme Court strikes down IEEPA tariffs
description: The Supreme Court rules emergency-powers tariffs unlawful, removing the 10% fentanyl and reciprocal duties on China; a 10% Section 122 global tariff follows days later.
source: Supreme Court; China Briefing; NYT, Feb 20-24 2026

description: Jensen Huang's GTC 2026 keynote in San Jose showcases the Vera Rubin platform as Nvidia's next-generation AI system following Blackwell.
Chinese authorities reportedly approve H200 purchases for select domestic customers, clearing the final regulatory hurdle for Nvidia's first major China data-center sales since 2025.

event: US halts tool shipments to Hua Hong
description: Commerce reportedly orders Lam Research, Applied Materials and KLA to halt chipmaking-equipment shipments to Chinese foundries Hua Hong and Huali.
Trump visits Beijing for a two-day summit with Xi, attended by Jensen Huang; few concrete outcomes and no announcement on H200 imports.
source: CNBC; Asia Society; China Briefing, May 14-15 2026

description: USTR imposes a 12.5% Section 301 tariff on Chinese goods over forced labor, effective July 24, adding friction ahead of Xi's planned US visit.
He Lifeng meets Bessent and Greer in New York; the sides establish a US-China AI Dialogue and operationalize a bilateral Board of Trade.
Xi Jinping makes a state visit to Washington; Bessent says the Busan truce is extended to January 2027 as negotiators reach a 'new joint arrangement.'

event: China may let Alibaba buy new Nvidia chips
description: Bloomberg, citing The Information, reports Beijing is weighing letting Alibaba and ByteDance buy some new Nvidia RTX AI chips, signaling a possible reopening.
